name: Zapoteco de Santa Catarina Quioquitani
catalog_citation: Ward, Michael; Emiliano Zurita Sánchez; y Stephen A. Marlett. 2008 [edición preliminar corregida 30-mayo-2016]. Zapoteco de Santa Catarina Quioquitani. Ilustraciones fonéticas de lenguas amerindias, ed. Stephen A. Marlett. Lima: SIL International y Universida…
catalog_quote: 4. Acento prosódico. Las raíces de las palabras de clase mayor se acentúan. El acento prosódico tiene un efecto en la pronunciación de las vocales en ciertos contextos (véase Convenciones). ... [§5] Una vocal modal acentuada es fonéticamente laringalizada, un poco alargada, y seguida por una breve oclusiva glotal con soltura, cuando se presenta en posición final de la frase: / m á / [ ˈm á̰ ˑ ˀ ă̰ ] ma ‘animal’ ... Los pronombres enclíticos y los demostrativos enclíticos no se acentúan y por lo tanto esta oclusiva glotal no se presenta con ellos ... [§1] El zapoteco de Santa Catarina Quioquitani tiene raíces monosilábicas, a diferencia de otras variantes de la región que preservan las raíces bisilábicas del proto-Zapoteco ... [§3] Se presentan tres tonos fonémicos superficialmente: Alto, Bajo y Ascendente (Bajo-Alto).

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every quoted clause is verbatim in the held PDF at the pages given (§4 p.6, §5 p.7, §1 p.1, §3 p.5); the held PDF is byte-identical to the current lengamer.org file. (2) Deciding source: a 2008/2016 SIL phonetic illustration (phonology-article/sketch class) by the principal fieldworker, a native speaker and a phonologist; Glottolog 5.1 lists it as the sole descriptive reference for quio1241, and neither Glottolog's full bib (5 ztq items) nor SIL Mexico's own archive listing (14 items) contains a grammar, phonology monograph, dissertation or instrumental study. It is therefore the best available description, and its statement (major-class roots stressed; roots monosyllabic; enclitic pronouns/demonstratives unstressed; three tones) directly supports the MORPHOLOGICAL (root-stress) coding. sources.quote: Bibliographic only: Ilustración 2008; Ward 1987; Vocabulario del zapoteco de Quioquitani (Ward 2009, 103 pp draft ms, archive 29557); Oraciones ilustrativas (2006, 29561); Textos interlineales (2006, 29562); literacy booklets 1985-1991. No grammar or phonology beyond the Ilustración.

sources.citation: Ward, Michael. 1987. A focus particle in Quioquitani Zapotec. S.I.L.-Mexico Workpapers 9: 26-32. (Rosetta Project excerpt, Internet Archive item rosettaproject_ztq_phon-1: the phoneme footnote p.26 + issue TOC)
sources.quote: Lists the phonemes, simple vs laryngealized nuclei, and 'contrastive tones, not written in the practical orthography: high, low, low rising and mid rising' (four tones vs the Ilustración's three). Says nothing about stress/accent.

sources.citation: Marlett, Stephen A. & Michael Ward. n.d. The phonology and morphology of Quioquitani Zapotec. Unpublished manuscript, 48 pp. (Glottolog ref 308887, src 'otomanguean' bibliography; 'Trabajo inédito')

sources.note: Only fuller phonology+morphology treatment of this language on record (48 pp vs the 9-pp Ilustración our coding rests on); would state the root-stress rule with the morphology (prefixes, enclitics, compounds, Spanish loans) and settle whether any polysyllabic native words exist that could show non-root stress.
